title: How to Get a 7 in IB Business Management
summary: Learn how to get a 7 in IB Business Management with an 8-week study plan, command-term guidance, paper strategies, and practical IA advice.
body_markdown:
Getting a 7 in IB Business Management requires more than memorizing definitions. You need accurate subject knowledge, consistent application to unfamiliar businesses, reliable quantitative work, balanced evaluation, and a strong Business Research Project. The most effective approach is to study according to the assessment objectives, practise each paper's demands, and use feedback to eliminate recurring errors.


This guide explains how to get a 7 at SL or HL, including command terms, examination strategy, the internal assessment, and a realistic 8-week study plan.


### Understand what a 7 requires


A 7 is awarded from your **weighted total across all assessment components** , not from one examination score. Grade boundaries are set for each examination session, so no fixed percentage guarantees a 7 every year.


The current course, first assessed in 2024, uses this structure:


Component SL HL Main demand


Paper 1 35%, 1 hour 30 minutes 25%, 1 hour 30 minutes Pre-released context, unseen case, application and evaluation


Paper 2 35%, 1 hour 30 minutes 30%, 1 hour 45 minutes Unseen stimulus with a quantitative focus


Paper 3 Not assessed 25%, 1 hour 15 minutes Social enterprise and strategic recommendation


Business Research Project 30% 20% Real organizational issue investigated through a conceptual lens


These weightings are confirmed in the official[IB Business Management SL subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/dp/pdfs/business-management-sl-subject-brief-en.pdf) and[HL subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/dp/pdfs/business-management-hl-subject-brief-en.pdf) . SL students cannot neglect the research project because it contributes **30%** . HL students must prepare thoroughly for Paper 3 because it contributes **25%** .


### Study according to the assessment objectives


The assessment objectives describe what examinations and coursework measure. Content-only revision prepares you for AO1 but not for all the skills that distinguish top responses.


Assessment objective What it assesses What a top student does


**AO1: Knowledge and understanding** Business tools, theories, concepts and issues Uses accurate terminology and precise definitions


**AO2: Application and analysis** Applying theory and data to business situations Uses case evidence and develops cause-and-effect reasoning


**AO3: Synthesis and evaluation** Weighing alternatives and stakeholder interests Reaches a balanced, evidence-based judgment


**AO4: Use and application of appropriate skills** Quantitative work, research and communication Shows calculations, selects suitable tools and structures answers clearly


Highlight knowledge, application, analysis and evaluation in different colours when reviewing an answer. If an extended response contains mostly definitions and general advantages, it is not yet operating at the level required for top marks.


### Master the command terms


A command term identifies the intellectual task you must perform. Misreading it can limit your mark even when your business knowledge is correct.


Command term Required response


**Define** Give the precise meaning of a term


**State** Give a brief, direct answer


**Describe** Give a detailed account of characteristics or events


**Explain** Show why or how something happens


**Analyse** Break an issue into parts and explain relationships or consequences


**Discuss** Present a balanced review supported by evidence


**Evaluate** Weigh strengths and limitations before reaching a judgment


**Recommend** Select and justify an advisable action


**Calculate** Obtain a numerical answer and show relevant working


Before writing, identify the command term, the business issue, and the scope imposed by the case. The[RevisionDojo guide to IB command terms](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-exam-command-terms-list) provides additional practice guidance.


For an **explain** question, develop a causal chain. For example, lower prices may increase demand by making a product affordable to more customers, potentially raising sales volume. For **evaluate** or **recommend** , consider both benefits and limitations before giving a justified conclusion. State the preferred option, the decisive factor, and any condition that could change your judgment.


### Build knowledge that can be applied


The syllabus contains five units: introduction to business management, human resource management, finance and accounts, marketing, and operations management. You must also understand **change, creativity, ethics and sustainability** , together with the business management toolkit.


For each theory, strategy or tool, create a compact revision entry containing:


- A precise definition
- Important advantages and limitations
- Conditions under which it is suitable
- Stakeholders likely to benefit or lose
- One useful indicator or short example


Do not learn only that market penetration means selling more existing products in existing markets. Understand that it may involve competitive pricing or promotion, can exploit existing capabilities, and may reduce margins or provoke competitors. This lets you apply the Ansoff matrix rather than merely identify a strategy.


Use[IB Business Management Study Notes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-business-management) to repair specific gaps, then retrieve the idea without looking. Flashcards suit definitions, formulas and framework components, but they cannot replace extended-response practice.


### Develop case-study application


Generic writing is a major barrier to a 7. Application means using details that affect the argument, not repeatedly inserting the company's name.


Suppose a small organic drinks company has limited cash, depends on one local supplier and plans to enter a foreign market. An applied recommendation would address its financial constraints, supply risk and limited international experience. Saying that expansion simply “increases sales and profits” ignores the decision's context.


Use this sequence for analytical paragraphs:


1. Make a relevant business point.
2. Select a precise fact or figure from the stimulus.
3. Explain the resulting business consequence.
4. Link that consequence to an objective or stakeholder.
5. Add a limitation or condition when evaluation is required.


Use the[IB Business Management Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-business-management/questionbank) to target weak topics or skills. After marking, rewrite the weakest paragraph before attempting another question.


### Make quantitative work dependable


Paper 2 has a strong quantitative focus, although calculations can support arguments elsewhere. Important areas include profitability, cash flow forecasts, break-even analysis, investment appraisal, efficiency and liquidity ratios, labour measures, capacity utilization, decision trees, and sales forecasting.


For every calculation, write the formula, substitute the figures, show intermediate steps and include units. Then interpret the result. If the margin of safety is 600 units, explain what this indicates about the distance between current output and break-even output and why that matters for risk.


Keep a formula error log recording the method, mistake, correct procedure and interpretation. Retest errors within 48 hours and again one week later.


### Use a paper-specific strategy


### Paper 1


The pre-released statement provides background for an unseen case study. Research unfamiliar contextual topics, but do not try to predict exact questions or memorize a fictional narrative.


Prepare definitions of unfamiliar terms, links to Units 1-5, relevant stakeholders, strategic tensions, course concepts, and tools that could analyse likely decisions. Paper 1 is the same examination for SL and HL and does not assess HL extension content. The official[IB Business Management curriculum update](https://www.ibo.org/university-admission/latest-curriculum-updates/business-management/) explains the role of the pre-released statement and unseen case.


### Paper 2


Practise selecting formulas without being told which one to use. After every result, ask what it means for the organization. Extended responses should combine numerical data, qualitative evidence and an explicit judgment.


Allocate time approximately in proportion to marks and reserve several minutes for checking. Do not sacrifice an extended answer by overworking a low-mark question.


### Paper 3 at HL


Paper 3 assesses a social enterprise and culminates in a strategic plan of action. Your recommendation must address the identified human need and the organization's financial and operational sustainability.


Use evidence across the resources and propose an implementable plan covering actions, sequencing, finance, stakeholders, risks and measures of success. Social purpose and financial sustainability are not opposites because a social enterprise normally requires both.


### Strengthen the Business Research Project


The internal assessment is a research project of no more than **1,800 words** about a real issue or problem facing a specific organization. SL and HL students complete the same task using one conceptual lens: **change, creativity, ethics or sustainability** .


A strong project needs a focused research question, credible supporting documents, relevant business tools, evidence-based analysis, consistent use of the conceptual lens, and a conclusion that answers the question directly. It should also evaluate uncertainty, source limitations and competing stakeholder interests.


Do not insert every available tool. One well-used force field analysis or ratio analysis is more valuable than several decorative frameworks. Consult the[RevisionDojo Business Management IA guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ia-guides/ib-business-management) , while treating your teacher and current official documentation as the final authorities.


### A realistic 8-week IB Business study plan


Plan five sessions each week, normally **60-75 minutes** each. HL students should add a weekly Paper 3 block of about 45 minutes.


Week Main focus Required output


1 Diagnostic assessment and Unit 1 Timed set, weakness map and corrected answers


2 Human resource management Retrieval cards and two applied responses


3 Finance and accounts Four quantitative drills and a timed Paper 2 section


4 Marketing Case comparison and one 10-mark response


5 Operations management Tool-selection drills and one mixed case set


6 Concepts, toolkit and weak topics Three improved evaluative paragraphs


7 Full-paper practice Timed Papers 1 and 2, plus Paper 3 for HL


8 Final consolidation Error-log retests, formula recall and a final simulation


Each week should combine content repair, retrieval, case-study questions, quantitative or extended-response practice, and timed work followed by corrections. Jojo AI can explain why a paragraph is descriptive rather than analytical, but write the first attempt independently. Use Mock Exams or Predicted Papers for timing and stamina, not as forecasts of exact questions. The[RevisionDojo Business Management coverage guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-ib-business-management-coverage) explains how notes, flashcards, questions and feedback can form one revision cycle.


### Common mistakes that prevent a 7


- **Memorizing model answers:** Unseen cases require adaptation.
- **Using the company name as application:** Real application uses data, objectives and circumstances.
- **Listing advantages and disadvantages:** Analysis requires developed consequences, while evaluation requires judgment.
- **Ignoring units or working:** Method may earn marks even when the final answer is wrong.
- **Writing repetitive conclusions:** Resolve the decision and explain its conditions.
- **Leaving timed practice until the final week:** Knowledge must be accessible under pressure.
- **Treating the IA as a company report:** It must investigate a real issue through a conceptual lens.


### Conclusion


To get a 7 in IB Business Management, convert precise knowledge into case-specific analysis, accurate calculations and justified decisions. Prepare each component according to its weighting, master the command terms, and use an error log to turn feedback into measurable improvement.
